source: Original items built on the five self-knowledge questions in Peter Drucker, 'Managing Oneself' (Harvard Business Review, 1999): How do I perform? How do I learn? What are my values? Where do I belong? What should I contribute? Learning is asked from evidence, not self-guessing: three real moments of fast learning and one that didn't stick; the way that shows up most is the result. Values uses Drucker's mirror test and a real clash. Contribution asks what the situation needs and what result in 18 months would matter. D3 and D8 extend the reader/listener question to how a person wants information shaped and delivered, so AI agents can brief them the way they take it in.

items.say: When someone needs to bring you up to speed on something important, what works best for you?

options.text: Send it to me in writing; I take it in best by reading
Tell me; I take it in best by listening
Talk me through it, then send it in writing

items.question: perform

items.say: When information reaches you, what do you want first?

options.text: The bottom line, with detail only if I ask
The whole picture, start to finish
A picture: a diagram, a table, an example

items.question: perform

items.say: When an AI or a teammate reports back to you, what works best?

options.text: A short written message I can read in a minute
A voice note or a quick call
A page I can come back to, with everything in one place

items.question: perform

items.say: Where do you do your best work?

options.text: Alone, with time to think
With one close partner
In a team, bouncing off people

items.question: perform

items.say: Which role brings out your best?

options.text: The one who makes the call
The trusted advisor to the one who makes the call
Either, depending on the subject

items.question: perform

items.say: When do you do your best work?

options.text: Under pressure, close to a deadline
With structure and plenty of lead time
A steady rhythm, the same every day

items.say: Think of a real time you picked something up fast at work. Picture the moment it clicked. How did it reach you?

options.text: I read about it
Someone explained it to me out loud
I watched someone do it
I just did it, tried and adjusted
I wrote it out in my own words
I talked it through or taught it to someone

options.text: I read about it
Someone explained it to me out loud
I watched someone do it
I just did it, tried and adjusted
I wrote it out in my own words
I talked it through or taught it to someone

items.question: learn
items.say: One more: something you understood quickly in the past year. How did it get in?

options.text: I read about it
Someone explained it to me out loud
I watched someone do it
I just did it, tried and adjusted
I wrote it out in my own words
I talked it through or taught it to someone

items.question: learn

options.text: I read about it

I watched someone do it

items.question: values
items.say: At the end of a working day, what do you most need to see in the mirror?

options.text: That I was honest, even when it cost me
That I made a real difference to someone
That the work was excellent, not just done
That I stayed free and true to my own way
That I grew, and pushed past my edge

items.question: values
items.say: Think of a time work asked something of you that felt wrong, or a place you left or wanted to leave. What was at stake?

options.text: Honesty: cutting corners or bending the truth
How people were treated
Quality: being asked to ship work below my standard
Short-term money over the long game
Control: not being trusted to do it my way
Nothing like that has happened to me
A small team where everyone does a bit of everything
A larger organization with clear roles
On my own, with people I bring in when needed

items.question: belong
items.say: Think of the place or project where you did your best work so far. What made it fit?

options.text: The people I worked with
A mission I believed in
Freedom to do it my way
A hard challenge at a fast pace
Clear goals and a clear structure

items.question: contribute
items.say: Look at your work as it is right now, not what you'd like to do. What does it need most from you?

options.text: A new idea or a clear direction
The right people brought in and on board
The work itself done well and on time
A system so it runs without me
Money or deals brought in

items.question: contribute
items.say: Eighteen months from now, which result would make you say: that mattered?

options.text: Something I built is out in the world and people use it
A team or community that runs well and keeps going
A clear number reached: income, clients, growth
Specific people are better off because of me
I've become truly excellent at my craft
